name: GraphRAG (From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2404.16130, cs.CL); v1 24 Apr 2024, v2 19 Feb 2025. Not formally published at a peer-reviewed venue (technical report from Microsoft Research).
authors_affiliation: Darren Edge and Ha Trinh (co-first authors), Newman Cheng, Joshua Bradley, Alex Chao, Apurva Mody, Steven Truitt, Dasha Metropolitansky, Robert Osazuwa Ness, Jonathan Larson. Affiliations: Microsoft Research; Microsoft Strategic Missions and Technologies; Microsoft Office of the CTO.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/microsoft/graphrag (actively maintained official Microsoft open-source implementation; documentation at https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/)
task_domain: QA / query-focused summarization (global sensemaking question answering over private text corpora).
problem_setting: Offline-indexed, single-agent, non-interactive QA over a fixed private text corpus (~1 million token range). The goal is to answer global 'sensemaking' questions about an entire corpus (e.g., 'What are the main themes in the dataset?') that conventional vector RAG cannot handle because such questions are query-focused summarization (QFS) tasks rather than explicit retrieval tasks. No task-level supervision/labels; evaluation uses LLM-as-judge head-to-head comparisons plus claim-based metrics. Indexing is done once offline with an LLM; queries are answered at test time via map-reduce over precomputed community summaries.
what_is_retrieved: Pregenerated community summaries (report-like summaries of groups of closely related entities) derived from an LLM-built entity knowledge graph; the underlying graph index spans nodes (entities), edges (relationships), and covariates (claims). For the vector RAG baseline (SS), raw source text chunks are retrieved.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: an LLM-derived entity knowledge graph plus hierarchical community summaries built offline from the source documents. The store is frozen after offline indexing; it is not a growing/episodic agent memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Completeness/exhaustive-coverage objective rather than fixed top-k ranking. The hierarchical Leiden community partition is described as mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive (MECE), enabling divide-and-conquer global summarization in which ALL community summaries at a chosen level are processed (map-reduce over the whole partition), not a small top-k retrieved subset. At reduce time, partial answers are filtered/ranked by a 0-100 helpfulness score and added until the token budget is reached.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning system; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is positioned as graph-based RAG / query-focused summarization.
retrieval_unit: Community summary (report-like summary over a group of closely related entities = a graph community). Underlying graph index units are KG entities (nodes), relationships (edges), and claims (covariates). Baseline SS retrieves document text chunks (600-token chunks).
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: an LLM derives an entity knowledge graph from source documents, then community detection partitions it and the LLM pregenerates community summaries at all hierarchy levels at indexing time. The store is frozen after offline construction (no test-time growth).
index_structure_topology: Knowledge GRAPH plus HIERARCHICAL community structure: entities/relationships/claims form a graph; hierarchical Leiden community detection recursively partitions it into a nested hierarchy of communities (root level C0 -> C1 -> C2 -> leaf level C3), each level a MECE partition. Community summaries are organized bottom-up along this hierarchy.
retriever_type: LLM-as-retriever / generative (no learned dense or BM25 retriever in the global pipeline). At query time a map-reduce process uses the LLM to read all community summaries (generate partial answers + helpfulness scores) rather than a similarity-based retriever; relevance filtering is done by the LLM's 0-100 helpfulness score. The vector RAG baseline (SS) uses a conventional dense semantic-search retriever over text chunks.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The global GraphRAG pipeline uses no trained retriever; community selection is via LLM-generated helpfulness scores, not a learned similarity model. Graph construction relies on prompted LLM extraction (with self-reflection/gleaning), not retriever training.
query_construction: Raw user query used directly. The query is applied unchanged against each community summary in the map step (each summary independently produces a partial answer to the raw query); no query decomposition, expansion, or intent extraction is performed. (Separately, for benchmark construction, an LLM generates user personas, tasks, and high-level global questions, but this is evaluation-set generation, not query-time processing.)
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at query time): a single global query is answered in one map-reduce pass over a chosen community level; no per-step or trajectory-level query construction.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot (single map-reduce pass per query over precomputed community summaries at a fixed chosen level). Indexing-time summarization is precomputed offline; there is no iterative or uncertainty-triggered retrieval loop at query time.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval/use of context is not conditionally triggered. Every query deterministically runs the map step over all community summaries at the selected level; the only filtering signal is the LLM-assigned 0-100 helpfulness score per partial answer (answers scored 0 are filtered out).
reranking: Yes, a lightweight LLM-score-based ranking at the reduce step: intermediate community answers are sorted in descending order of LLM-generated helpfulness score (0-100) and iteratively added to the reduce context window until the token limit is reached. No cross-encoder or learned reranker is used.
retrieved_context_refinement: Map-reduce summarization with helpfulness-score filtering: in the map step the LLM produces partial answers with 0-100 helpfulness scores; answers scored 0 are filtered out; remaining answers are ranked and concatenated up to a token budget, then summarized into the global answer in the reduce step. Community summaries themselves are a form of pre-retrieval distillation/compression of the underlying graph elements.
index_content_separation: Partial: the hierarchical community structure separates lightweight higher-level (more abstract, fewer/shorter) summaries from heavier lower-level (more detailed, more numerous) summaries, allowing a user/query to scan general themes at one level then drill into linked lower-level reports; community summaries also act as a lightweight index over the heavier raw source text. Not a formal progressive-disclosure index-then-content protocol.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation via map-reduce query-focused summarization: each community summary is independently placed in the LLM context to generate a partial (community) answer with a helpfulness score (map); selected partial answers are then combined in a final context window and summarized into the global answer (reduce).
planning_integration: Plan-free; retrieve(precompute)-then-summarize. No agentic planning, tree search, or step-wise acting. The pipeline is a fixed two-stage map-reduce over precomputed community summaries: divide-and-conquer global summarization that decomposes the corpus by graph community (indexing time) and aggregates partial answers (query time).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer (no interleaving of retrieval with reasoning steps). A single map-reduce pass produces one global answer per query; there is no per-CoT-step, per-sentence, or per-tool-call retrieval.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled free-text report-style community summaries (natural-language summaries that aggregate node/edge/claim element summaries). Underlying injected information is abstractive LLM summaries of graph elements; the global answer is itself a generated free-text summary.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled abstractive summaries at multiple abstraction levels: hierarchical community summaries range from highly abstract corpus-wide themes (root C0) to fine-grained subtopic detail (leaf C3). These are abstractive summaries of concepts (entities, relationships, claims) rather than raw trajectories or single demonstrations.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Helpfulness-score filtering in the map step (LLM rates each partial answer 0-100; score-0 answers are dropped before the reduce step). At indexing time, a self-reflection 'gleaning' loop (iterative LLM re-prompting to detect missed entities/relationships) increases extraction completeness and reduces noise/omission. Random shuffling of community summaries across reduce chunks mitigates 'lost in the middle' positional bias.
memory_type: graph (entity knowledge graph) plus hierarchical community-summary store. Static after offline indexing; not an episodic or skill-library agent memory.
write_back: False (no test-time write-back). New experiences/cases are not stored during deployment; the graph index and community summaries are built once at indexing time and frozen. (The index can be rebuilt/extended offline, but the system does not write back from query answering.)
online_growth: No. The retrievable store (graph + community summaries) does not grow during deployment/test time; it is constructed offline and frozen.
write_back_trigger: Never (at query/test time). Index construction is an offline batch process, not triggered by query-time events; there is no on-success/on-failure/reflective write-back of answers into the store.
failure_experience_usage: Not applicable / not used. The system does not store or retrieve failed or negative experiences; there is no experience memory. (The only failure-like signal is filtering of score-0 partial answers within a single query, which are discarded, not stored.)
memory_evolution_update: Not applicable at runtime: the store is effectively static/append-built offline. Within indexing, repeated element instances of the same entity/relationship are aggregated/deduplicated and summarized (dedup-merge during construction), but no post-write mutation occurs during deployment.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/selection is not a learned or RL-optimized policy; community-answer selection is governed by LLM-generated helpfulness scores and a fixed map-reduce schedule, not a trained retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single, monolithic indexing+query pipeline; no multi-agent or cross-framework memory sharing (parallelism in map step is independent LLM calls, not cooperating agents with shared memory).
benchmarks: Two ~1M-token real-world datasets: (1) Podcast transcripts of 'Behind the Tech with Kevin Scott' (1669 x 600-token chunks, ~1M tokens); (2) News articles from the MultiHop-RAG news corpus (Tang & Yang, 2024), published Sept 2013-Dec 2023 (3197 x 600-token chunks, ~1.7M tokens). Evaluation set: LLM-generated global sensemaking questions (personas x tasks x questions), 125 questions per comparison. HotPotQA used only for a self-reflection/chunk-size ablation in the appendix.
benchmark_family: QA / query-focused summarization over long private corpora (global sensemaking). Not one of the standard agent/embodied/tool families; closest normalized grouping is long-document/corpus-level QA & summarization. News corpus is sourced from MultiHop-RAG.
baselines: Conventional vector RAG 'semantic search' (SS, retrieves text chunks up to a token budget); global text summarization without a graph index (TS, map-reduce applied directly to shuffled/chunked source texts). GraphRAG is evaluated at four community levels C0 (root), C1, C2, C3 (leaf). All six conditions (C0-C3, TS, SS) share the same context-window size and answer-generation prompts; they differ only in how the context window is populated.
key_metrics: LLM-as-judge head-to-head win rate (%) on four criteria: Comprehensiveness, Diversity, Empowerment, and Directness (a control criterion). Plus claim-based validation metrics (Experiment 2): Comprehensiveness = average number of unique factual claims per answer (extracted via Claimify); Diversity = average number of claim clusters per answer. Cost: context tokens per query.
headline_result: Using GPT-4 (gpt-4-turbo), global GraphRAG conditions substantially outperformed conventional vector RAG (SS): comprehensiveness win rates 72-83% (p<.001) on Podcast and 72-80% (p<.001) on News; diversity win rates 75-82% (p<.001) on Podcast and 62-71% (p<.01) on News. Root-level GraphRAG (C0) retained 72% comprehensiveness and 62% diversity win rates over vector RAG while requiring ~9x-43x fewer context tokens per query (>97% fewer tokens than source-text summarization TS).
ablations: Community level comparison (C0/C1/C2/C3): community summaries gave a small consistent comprehensiveness/diversity gain over source-text summarization (TS) except at root level (e.g., intermediate-level on Podcast 57% comprehensiveness win, low-level on News 64%); no statistically significant differences among global conditions or vs TS otherwise. Token-cost vs level tradeoff: C3 used 26-33% fewer context tokens than TS, C0 used >97% fewer. Self-reflection ('gleaning') ablation (Appendix A.2, on HotPotQA): iterative self-reflection lets larger chunk sizes recover entity references lost at 600 vs 2400 token chunks (GPT-4 extracted nearly 2x more entity references at 600 vs 2400 token chunks without reflection). Claim-based validation (Experiment 2) corroborates LLM-judge comprehensiveness/diversity findings.
evaluation_decoupling: No standard intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) are reported, since the global pipeline is not a top-k retrieval task. Instead, end-to-end answer-quality metrics (LLM-judge win rates) are validated by an independent claim-based intrinsic measure (claim count and claim-cluster count via Claimify) reported separately (Experiment 2).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-focused (final answer comprehensiveness/diversity/empowerment/directness). Claim-based measures add a finer-grained outcome decomposition (factual-claim coverage and diversity of an answer), but there is no step-wise retrieval/planning-accuracy or reasoning-faithfulness scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Token cost reported per condition (Table 2): map-reduce over source texts (TS) is most expensive (e.g., ~1.01M Podcast / ~1.71M News context tokens); root-level community summaries (C0) need dramatically fewer (~26.7k Podcast / ~39.8k News), i.e. ~9x-43x fewer tokens than TS and >97% reduction. Offline indexing cost: ~281 minutes for the Podcast dataset on a 16GB-RAM Xeon VM using a public gpt-4-turbo endpoint (2M TPM, 10k RPM). Tradeoff: root-level GraphRAG (C0) trades a modest quality drop for large query-time token savings.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed context window of 8k tokens for community summaries, community answers, and global answers; 600-token chunks (100-token overlap) for indexing and for the SS/TS text. At reduce time, community answers are reranked-then-truncated: sorted by helpfulness score and added until the token limit is reached (budget-capped). All six conditions share the same context-window size and prompts.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Evaluation questions are LLM-synthesized for global sensemaking: given a short corpus description, the LLM generates N user personas, K tasks per persona, and M high-level questions per (user,task) pair (K*N*M questions) that require global corpus understanding and explicitly avoid retrieval of specific low-level facts; 125 questions per head-to-head comparison, each repeated 5 times and averaged. Datasets are two ~1M-token corpora (Podcast ~1M tokens / 1669 chunks; News ~1.7M tokens / 3197 chunks). Answers are open-ended (no single gold answer); difficulty is assessed via LLM-judge win rates and claim-based metrics rather than exact-match accuracy.
builds_on: Retrieval-augmented generation (Lewis et al., 2020); hierarchical/recursive summarization indexing (RAPTOR, Sarthi et al., 2024; Kim et al., 2023); graph community detection (Leiden, Traag et al., 2019; Louvain, Blondel et al., 2008; graph modularity, Newman, 2006) implemented via the graspologic library; LLM self-reflection/gleaning (Reflexion-style, Shinn et al., 2024; Madaan et al., 2024); LLM-based persona generation for evaluation; Claimify (Metropolitansky & Larson, 2025) for claim extraction; MultiHop-RAG news corpus (Tang & Yang, 2024).
contrasts_with: Conventional vector/semantic-search RAG ('vector RAG', SS), which fails on global sensemaking queries; prior query-focused summarization (QFS) methods that do not scale to RAG-scale corpora; non-graph hierarchical-summary indexing methods (e.g., RAPTOR / Sarthi et al., 2024; Kim et al., 2023), from which GraphRAG differs by building a graph index and using graph-community detection for thematic partitioning; fact-retrieval benchmarks (HotPotQA, MultiHop-RAG, MT-Bench) and vector-RAG-oriented evaluation frameworks (e.g., RAGAS criteria).
lineage: Group B (RAG for task solving) / static-corpus document-graph RAG. A foundational 2024 work establishing the graph + community-summary (graph/community retrieval unit) line of 'GraphRAG' methods for global/sensemaking QA, distinct from experience/case-memory agent lines; spawned a large family of follow-up graph-based RAG systems.
